claim: When certificates in the certificate list match the client hostname but none of them is compatible with the client, the TLS handshake fails and the load balancer does not fall back to the default certificate.
question: When does an ALB use the default certificate instead of one from the certificate list?

values.display: does not fall back to the default certificate

evidence.quote: If none of the matched certificates is compatible with the client, the handshake fails. The load balancer does not fall back to the default certificate.

claim: A Gateway Load Balancer operates at the third layer of the OSI model, the network layer; listens for all IP packets across all ports, and forwards traffic to the target group with the GENEVE protocol on port 6081.
question: At which OSI layer does a Gateway Load Balancer work, and what traffic does it listen for?

values.display: listens for all IP packets across all ports

evidence.quote: A Gateway Load Balancer operates at the third layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model, the network layer.

A Gateway Load Balancer operates at the third layer of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) model. It listens for all IP packets across all ports and forwards traffic to the target group that's specified in the listener rule, using the GENEVE protocol on port 6081.
